sourceInformation.source: Space Fortress (Century Electronics / CVS, 1981); excludes the Astrocade and cognitive-training games.
sourceInformation.perspective: Overhead free flight and fortress defense; side-view ground firing line
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), JavaScript/HTML/CSS and Web Audio; AI Hub protocol 1, client 1.4.0 (35a1047). Fully embedded.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Native shaded procedural pixel art: custom ships, fortress/radiators, boss, carriages, gravity fields and continuous-location backgrounds.
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.anim sprites plus simulation-driven thrust, recoil, hit, pulse, docking, retreat and victory.
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized score, effects and gibberish radio on engine buses. Music defaults to 10%. Signal tested; human listening unknown.
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 couch pilots standalone; 1–4 authoritative shared-world AI Hub co-op with dedicated hosting and bounded local movement prediction.
sourceInformation.testing: Seeded complete campaigns, native headless rendering, simulated pads/touch, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, audio signals, official and deep Hub checks. Hardware and listening unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Inspected Century flyer, sampled Century gameplay footage, Museum entry, cached MobyGames account, MAME CVS, and pinned engine/Hub sources. See docs/research.md.

testingFeedback: 30 unique issues found through automated checks, visual inspection and code review; all fixed. See docs/issues.md.
3 were critical: simultaneous outcome priority, desktop canvas sizing, and low-DPI arena cropping.
Complete normal-input campaign playthroughs and the simultaneous failure regression proved the game can be won without attract cheats.
Syntax checks were least informative: successful parsing alone cannot establish playability or visual clarity.
engineFeedback: Native pixel/sprite tools, exact headless fixed stepping, Shell controls and procedural audio buses fit the arcade siege well.
Settings redefinition needed preserved native metadata; the minimum pixel scale needed a scoped adapter to fit low-DPI portrait screens.
The deterministic three-act simulation, authored encounter director and authoritative cooperative replication.
Coordinating native menu/input lifecycle with separately serialized shared-world state and reliable audio cleanup.
No vendor engine changes. Added game-level adapters for fractional arena fit, dev slider units and non-P1 refit navigation.
Expose stoppable source handles returned by custom audio instruments through the SFX/music lifecycle.
promptFeedback: The connected defense layers give the game a distinctive structure and a concrete ending.
Several unrelated games share the source name; explicitly selecting Century resolved the ambiguity.
Making couch, touch, controller and authoritative online play use one coherent simulation.
Keep the acceptance gates, but distinguish mandatory deliverables from suggested implementation paths.

aiHub.name: Space Fort After Dark
aiHub.description: Command a Viper through a three-act night siege. Break gravity anchors, cool Fortress 13, and dock into the final gun line to bring down the siege ship.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD move; right stick/mouse aim; R2/click fire; L2/Space boost; Square/E pulse; Options/Escape pause.
